title: [WT-03b] Daemon: landingRetry hardening (board-echo denylist, release routing)
description:
WT-19's planner (architect-4ae016fb) split this row out of WT-19's whole-epic hardening. It carries the two findings WT-03's planner (architect-899a90d6) handed to WT-19 in comment-631323b2. WT-03 (task-9a39bf6a2c4444b4b0799cd16dc2a9f1) adds Task.landingRetry. This row closes two gaps around that field before the WT-11 wrapper resume (task-dd1ee586b90d4fc785434454b1423e76), which depends on this row, relies on it.

Objective: a landingRetry set by the daemon survives board echoes, and releasing a seat mid-retry never hands QA a task with nothing landed.

Deliverable:
1. packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts: add 'landingRetry' to UPDATE_TASK_DENYLIST.
   - The daemon owns the field; only finalize_attempt writes it.
   - Without this, a stale full-task board echo could restore a cleared landingRetry, causing a spurious LANDING-RETRY or an early BLOCKED.
   - A board client could also forge one.
2. packages/moe-daemon/src/state/workerLifecycle.ts, nextStatusForRelease:
   - A WORKING task with landingRetry set stays WORKING on requeue, even when every step is COMPLETED.
   - Today that case goes to REVIEW, handing QA a task whose completion never landed.
   - park still goes to BACKLOG.
   - A task without landingRetry keeps today's routing.
   - Widen the Pick<Task, ...> parameter to include landingRetry. Callers in sweeps.ts, workerStore.ts, releaseTask.ts and taskStore.ts already pass full tasks; check each one.
3. Tests: one WebSocketServer.test.ts case, and release cases in the existing release tests (releaseTask.test.ts or workerStore.test.ts).

NOT in scope:
- finalize_attempt's own routing (WT-03)
- the wrapper resume (WT-11)
- docs (WT-17)

Verification: cd packages/moe-daemon && npm run build && npx vitest run src/server/WebSocketServer.test.ts src/tools/releaseTask.test.ts src/state/workerStore.test.ts
definitionOfDone: WebSocketServer.test.ts: a board UPDATE_TASK carrying landingRetry (an object or null) leaves the task's stored landingRetry unchanged, while the message's other allowed fields still apply.

releaseTask.test.ts or workerStore.test.ts: releasing (requeue) a WORKING task with every step COMPLETED and landingRetry set leaves it WORKING and unassigned. The same task without landingRetry still goes to REVIEW. Park still goes to BACKLOG.
The verification command in the description exits 0.

comments.content:
Governor, 18:48Z. IMPORTANT for whoever runs this row's final gate. Do NOT run `(cd packages/moe-daemon && npm run build && …)` in the shared checkout (D:\projexts\moes or /mnt/d/projexts/moes).
- `prebuild` deletes dist first. The live daemon runs from that dist.
- From WSL the build then fails, because the shared node_modules are Windows-native: tsx exits 1, and tsc can't resolve @typescript/typescript-linux-x64. dist is left deleted.
- This already happened once today (about 15:31Z). The governor restored dist at 18:45Z. The prebuild fix is task-f9789178.

Run the same gate in an isolated snapshot instead: a git archive or clone of HEAD outside the repo with your files overlaid, native deps, MOE_* unset (mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate). This comment overrides the plan text on that point.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
# Protect landingRetry at board and release boundaries
Goal: preserve daemon-owned retry state and keep an unlanded completed-step task in the worker queue. Architecture: reuse UPDATE_TASK_DENYLIST and the single nextStatusForRelease routing function; no parallel policy or new schema. Tech: TypeScript/Node.js, Vitest, existing ws integration fixtures.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Verified UPDATE_TASK filters Object.entries through UPDATE_TASK_DENYLIST before state.updateTask; existing evidence-label tests show the right pattern. nextStatusForRelease currently picks only status/implementationPlan and sends all-completed WORKING tasks to REVIEW after the park check. releaseTask has both assigned release and unassigned repair paths that call it. workerStore, sweeps, taskStore and unblockWorker also pass whole tasks. WT-03's submitted producer contract is Task.landingRetry?: LandingRetry|null with reason,paths,rescueRef,targetTip,count,at; it has not landed yet, so use that landed type rather than adding it here. Memory mem:convention-daemon-owned-task-field-ws-denylist requires asserting forwarded payload keys too, because downstream sanitization can otherwise mask missing transport guards.
planningNotes.risks: One narrow two-boundary field protection fix, four files / approximately 35 minutes, under 400 net LOC. Full daemon regression is appropriate for the shared lifecycle signature/routing change in addition to the task's named focused command; epic rail also requires parity. No launcher, schema, finalization, resume or docs edits. Preserve error handling and all non-WORKING/park routing. Test both assigned release and already-unassigned repair, so the latter cannot silently re-promote a retry to QA. Existing files clean during exploration; retain unrelated shared dirt. Portable existing fs/path temp fixtures; no platform-specific logic.
